text:
Trevor Zegras is still on Philadelphia's top power-play unit with Matvei Michkov, and eight of his 15 points have come with the extra man. At even strength, the picture is rougher. The Flyers get only 38.02% of expected goals at 5v5 with him on the ice, and they are 8.8 points worse than when he sits. For a player Evolving-Hockey had in the 94th percentile at driving play last season, that is the number to watch.

Some of it is bad luck. Philadelphia has scored 4.8 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on, which has cost him assists, and his own shooting is a little under his range: five goals on 6.75 expected. His own chances are up to 0.95 expected goals per 60, from 0.81 last season.

He has five points in his last ten games, the latest a one-timer off Tyson Foerster's feed in Saturday's comeback win in Columbus. The skill on the power play is not the question. Whether his 5v5 minutes stop bleeding chances against is.
headline: Trevor Zegras and the Flyers' underwater minutes
